title: Time Keys Sailor Pluto
description:
For my Sailor Pluto Cosplay, I wanted my belt keys to have my own touch, in the manga they are often drawn incredibly flat. This takes away the belief of them being keys, with that in mind I took multiple Manga clips where we see the keys and modeled each one in its own unique style. Rather than being super flat "keys" they have an appearance more akin to skeleton key shapes and styles. I hope you guys enjoy these!!


-BUILDING NOTES-
Pluto's keys are thankfully quite simple compared to other small trinkets, however, they are still rather fragile. When printing these keys I heavily recommend printing them fully solid, or with at least an infill above 80.

Included in your download is a zip file containing each individual key, with their current size they can be printed on most printers but can be cut without much hassle.

Please do not redistribute or resell. They are intended for personal use only. Commercial use must buy a new copy for each item produced.

If you use the file please give us a shout on your posts using the @StarFall.cos or #StarFallProps tags, we'd love to see your work and show some love in return!!

title: MIni Drak RamAir Full Kit v3.5 2023
description:
Contents include:
1- 2 piece Battery Bay Cover
1-SMA Side Bay cover (print 2)
1-Electronics Bay Cover
1-Threaded RW Bulkhead

Needed:
- 1mm fiberglass rod or carbon rod
- goop or welders adhesive
- 2 thumb screws can be printed from ( https://www.thingiverse.com/thing:2431495 )

Installation Process:

Sand and rough up the sides and bottom of the bulkhead for the glue to adhere nicely to the material.

Bulkhead needs to be gooped in around the front main spar with a good amount of glue to adhere around the main spar, sides, and bottom of the bulkhead.
Channel is already cut out on the bottom right of the bulkhead big enough to run any wires needed to provide power and video to fpv cam.

Bay Covers:
Side bays are hinged using a 1mm spar thru the provided hole.
cut spars down so they fit from the side of the fuselage up to the spar channel next to the battery bay

Slice foam to embed the spar into the foam using goop or welders adhesive to keep the spar in place.
DO NOT GLUE THE SPAR INTO THE HOLE IN THE BAY COVER, THIS WILL NOT ALLOW THE COVER TO HINGE PROPERLY.

Battery Bay Cover:
The battery bay cover is in 2 pieces so anyone with a decent printer can print it out. printed on my ender 3 pro 235x235 size bed. These can be printed at the same time

Where the 2 pieces meet there is a provided hole for a 1mm spar to hinge the main bay from the glued part.
1mm spar should not be glued into the holes. Leaving about 4-5 mm on each side to be cut and glued into the foam for extra support at the hinge.
These 2 pieces are a tight enough fit to try and hide (as much as I could) the seam between the 2 and still have the ability to give access to the battery bay with zero issues.

Turn geometry into wearable fashion with this earrings and necklace set inspired by Archimedean solids! Bold yet lightweight, these pieces add a playful and elegant twist to any outfit.

Fashion lovers can print in polished gold or silver tones for a refined look, soft hues for a dreamy vibe, or bold neon colors for something modern and fun. The geometry catches the light beautifully, making every angle sparkle.

These accessories are more than jewelry—they’re wearable sculptures, merging the world of math with the art of style in a uniquely personal way.


About Archimedean Solids

Archimedean solids are a family of 13 remarkable polyhedra, admired for their symmetrical beauty and mathematical harmony. Unlike Platonic solids, their faces are made of more than one type of polygon, creating unique and fascinating patterns. They’ve inspired artists, architects, and designers for centuries. With 3D printing, these timeless shapes can now be transformed into jewelry, décor, and accessories—bringing mathematical elegance into everyday life.

- Charging port dimensions for Lightning/USB-A and Lightning/USB-C cable.
- Two thickness versions.
- In case of adding a rear camera protector, it is preferable to use the V1 version due to its thickness that aligns with the camera protector.

**WARNING!** Due to the design, it is not intended to be printed with non-flexible filament (PLA, ABS, PETG, etc). It is under your responsibility, and if you try it, do not hesitate to leave your comment on how it went with your experiment :)

Files are included in a Zip file.

Designed in 2 versions depending of the thickness you want!

**V1: Back thickness is 2.5mm**

Pros
- Extra protection on the back of the case
- Depending on the print settings, it can be printed with a specific infill to vary the flexibility and protection of the case.
- Better wraps around the device to resist drop impacts

Cons
- Larger printing time.
- More filament is required (gr).
- Thicker.

**V2: Back thickness is 1.5mm**

Pros
- Less printing time.
- Less filament is required (gr).
- Thinner.

Cons
- Less protection on the back of the case.
- Can't add fill pattern on the back of the case.
- Less protection for the camera

**Iphone Flexible Cases**
- [**Iphone 11 Pro Flexible Case**](https://cults3d.com/en/3d-model/various/iphone-11-pro-flexible-case)

title: Adjustable 3D Printed LED Bar
description:
Compatible & Scalable Design: The bar is 1500 mm (1.5 m) long with a rotatable structure. It can be extended or shortened as needed. (You can split it in your slicer using the cutting tool, or contact me to request files tailored to your printer and custom dimensions.)

Fully 3D Printed: The product is 100% 3D printed. For assembly, you only need wood screws suitable for your shelf, plus M5x35 screws and M5 nuts depending on the length. (Note: For 1.5 m length, 4 holders are enough, meaning 4 screws + 4 nuts. If you extend or shorten the bar, the number of holders will change accordingly.)

Easy Assembly: The files include M5 screw caps. No glue is required—just press-fit them firmly by hand or use a clamp.

Adjustable Holders: The sliding holder design allows you to secure the bar at any point you want.

Durable Build: Designed to withstand high forces. Some parts may require extra strength during assembly due to tight tolerances.

Print Settings: For maximum strength, an infill of 80%–100% is recommended.

Customizable: Cable holes are not included in the standard design, but I can create a custom revision for your needs if requested.



Uyumlu ve Ölçeklenebilir Tasarım: Bar uzunluğu 1500 mm’dir (1.5 m) ve dönebilir yapıdadır. İsteğe göre uzatılabilir veya kısaltılabilir. (Slicer’da kesme aracıyla parçalayabilir ya da benden özel ölçülerinize uygun dosya talep edebilirsiniz.)

Tamamen 3D Baskı: Ürün %100 3D baskıdır. Montaj için yalnızca rafınıza uygun sunta vidaları ile uzunluğa göre m5x35 vida ve m5 somun gerekir. (Not: 1.5 m uzunluk için 4 adet tutucu, yani 4 somun + 4 vida yeterlidir. Uzatma/kısaltmada sayı değişebilir.)

Pratik Montaj: Dosyalar içinde m5 vida kapakları mevcuttur. Kapaklar yapıştırıcı gerektirmez, yalnızca elle sıkıca ittirerek veya mengeneyle bastırarak takabilirsiniz.

Ayarlanabilir Tutucular: Sürgülü tasarım sayesinde barı istediğiniz noktadan sabitleyebilirsiniz.

Dayanıklı Yapı: Bar yüksek kuvvetlere dayanacak şekilde tasarlanmıştır. Bu nedenle bazı parçaların birleşimi ekstra güç gerektirebilir.

Baskı Ayarı: Sağlamlık için %80–%100 doluluk oranı önerilir.

Kişiselleştirilebilir: Kapak kısmında kablo delikleri standart olarak yoktur, ancak ihtiyacınıza göre özel tasarım revizyonu yapılabilir.

author: danifadriansyah
printing_settings:
i've printed all using PLA transparent colour. i've divided the object into 3 parts so that it will be easier to print and be able to apply different colour on different parts.
to make the ring, you need to print 1xgem.stl, 1xcrown.stl and 2xring.stl. be aware that i designed this in centimetre, the diameter of the ring is 20cm, so you need to scale it down to your own finger size.
to colour the gem parts, i painted a green colour marker onto the transparent PLA before feed it to the printer, so that the colour get fused with the PLA during print and it become permanent. for the crown i mixed the colour with black colour marker - as in picture (resulted dark green colour).
combine the 2 ring parts with super glue. i've painted the outer part of the gem parts using gold marker (coloured the same as the replica). the gem should be able to snap in tightly to the crown parts, you may apply some power glue to make it stay. then combine the crown and ring parts with power glue too .. now you have the green lantern's ring replica.
as you notice there is some space gap below the gem parts, you can slide in a green 0805 SMD led that soldered to a button battery CR-1616, to make it glowing like in the last photos.
i've included the SKP files, please feel free to edit it for adjustment purposes. and don't forget to leave comment if you like this design or if you can give me ideas on what to make next :)

title: Pokemon No. 376 Metagross
description:
Metagross 1:12 scale models from Pokemon video games, animated series, films and a trading card game.

All my Pokémon models are the same scale, so I recommend scaling up the smallest Pokémon in the slicer if your printer isn't perfectly calibrated. You can also scale down the largest ones, as some are very large.

The model marked "multicolor print" is an STL file, so after loading it into the slicer, you need to paint it. The coloring process is very simple. After selecting the "Fill" option, you select a color and click on a section of the model. It's as simple as coloring a picture in Paint. The "multicolor print" model is designed to color each body part individually, making the process quick and easy. If you have trouble finding this feature, let me know.

title: Orion's Belt Cocktail Table
description:
"Orion's Belt", an industrial modern cocktail table assembled from 3d prints and copper pipes.


Supplies:

• 0.5kg of filament
• 11ft of 1/2" copper pipe
    - x4 18"
    - x2 10"
    - x4 8"
    - x4 2"
• 41.5" of 1/4" copper pipe
    - x2 10.25"
    - x4 5.25"
• x4 1/2" copper pipe caps
• 12" x 12" sheet of 1/4" plexiglass
• x4 stylish #8 screws, 3/4" long, and matching washers


Instructions:

1) Print four copies each of both parts. I chose white PLA for a clean look, but a wood-based filament could also be attractive. My printer couldn't fit a whole piece at once, so I have also provided files to print each piece in half--in that case print four copies each of all the halves. If you print the halves, use an epoxy to glue the respective halves together.

2) Use a pipe cutter to create the quantity and lengths of pipe as listed above.

3) Assemble two layers of "Orion's Belt". A single layer is assembled using two each of the 3d printed parts. The 10" pipe goes down the middle, connecting two of the smaller parts. The other side of each smaller part is connected to a larger part using an 8" pipe. The 2" pipes protrude from the remaining side of the larger parts, and are each capped with a copper pipe cap. The smaller diameter copper pipes are used as cross braces: a 10.25" pipe runs across the middle, and two of the 5.25" pipes parallel this one on either side. Consult the pictures for the proper layout.

4) Using a skill saw, band saw, or router + jig, create a circle of the desired size from the sheet of plexiglass. I chose to leave no overhang on my Orion's Belt, which equated to a circle of diameter 11.75". I think an inch or two of overhang would also look nice, in which case you might need to start with a larger sheet of plexi (in fact I ordered a 12" x 12" plexi, but it arrived regretfully shorter in both dimensions).

5) Place your plexi on the flat side of one of the Orion's, and mark the locations designated for the #8 screws. Then drill through holes in the plexi. Be very careful on this step as drill bits like to travel and tear up your pristine plexi.

6) Affix the plexi to the flat side of one of the Orion's using the #8 screws and washers if desired. I used synthetic bronze screws and finishing washers for the matching effect.

7) Connect the two Orion's with the four 18" copper pipes. You'll probably want to epoxy these in place, but they'll hold fine without for demonstration porpoises! :)

8) Pour yourself a nice bourbon on the rocks, sit back, and dream about the stars while admiring your newest creation (after "liking" my entry of course).


#DAGOCULTS

title: Yet another Bezier library for OpenSCAD
description:
This is yet another Bezier library, which takes a list of nodes and control points and generates a list of points that you can then feed into polygon() or some other function. The Bezier curves can be either 2D or 3D, but I've only been using it for 2D.

The library is designed so one can lay out 2D Bezier curves basically in one's head. But if you prefer to lay them out graphically, you can use Inkscape plus [this plugin](https://www.thingiverse.com/thing:3527642) to design Bezier curves for this library.

One of the things I wanted was the ability to have an easy way to include smooth control points--control points that ensure that curve through the node has no cusp.

To use, first do `use <bezier.scad>;` and then call the function `Bezier(pointList)` to generate output points. There is an optional `precision=x` parameter. With that parameter, about `1/x` points will be generated per segment (excepting 2D segments that are a straight line--these are optimized to two points). Default is `precision=0.05`.

The `pointList` is a list of points arranged as follows:
`[node,control,control,node,control,control,node,...]`
I recommend that in your code you flag the control points with `/*C*/` so you don't get lost in a long list of points.

Each segment of the Bezier curve consists of two nodes, with two control points in between them. You can also have these special control points:

* `SYMMETRIC()`: This makes the control point be on the same line and at the same distance to the node as the control point on the other side

* `SMOOTH_REL(x)`: This is like `SYMMETRIC()` except that the distance of the control point to the node is `x` times the distance of the other control point to the node (can be negative for special effects); `SYMMETRIC()` is in fact shorthand for `SMOOTH_REL(1)`

* `SMOOTH_ABS(x)`: This is like `SYMMETRIC()` except that the distance of the control point to the node is exactly `x` (can be negative for special effects)

* `OFFSET(v)`: This makes the control point be at the neighboring node plus the vector `v`

* `POLAR(r,angle)`: Like `OFFSET(v)` but specified in polar coordinates; equivalent to `OFFSET(r*[cos(angle),sin(angle)])`; only works in 2D

* `SHARP()`: Puts the control point at the neighboring node; equivalent to `OFFSET([0,0])` (or `OFFSET([0,0,0])`)

You can't have `SMOOTH_*()` and/or `SYMMETRIC()` control points on _both_ sides of a node--the library then wouldn't know which line to place the control points on.

Finally, at the end of your list of points (and only there) you can add one or more `REPEAT_MIRRORED(normalVector)` points each of which stitches at the end of the path what came before but reflects it in the direction of the `normalVector`. For instance, if you want to draw a rounded plus sign, you can just include the first quarter, and then two `REPEAT_MIRRORED()` items.

There is also a utility function `DecodeSpecialBezierPoints(p)` which takes a node/control point list `p` and decodes all the special points (`SMOOTH_*()`, etc.) into ordinary 2D vectors. This is useful if, say, you want to take a Bezier curve and transform it in some way.

See the sample polygons in the source code for examples.

If you just want to use Bezier splines to smooth out the corner of a path, you can use:
`PathToBezier(path,offset=2,tension=0.551915024494,closed=false)`
This returns a Bezier path which rounds off each corner in the path at `offset` distance from the corner. The `tension` parameter specifies what fraction of the offset the control nodes are to be added at: the default is designed to make right angles be very close to circular arcs. You will still need to feed the resulting path into the `Bezier()` function to render it. 

Note that `REPEAT_MIRRORED()` can be used (multiple times if need be) at the end of the path fed into `PathToBezier`: this allows you to quickly build up more complex shapes. For instance, the rounded plus board for [a solitaire game](https://www.thingiverse.com/thing:4042748) can be generated with: `PathToBezier([[1,0],[1,1.5/3.5],[1.5/3.5,1.5/3.5],REPEAT_MIRRORED([-1,1]),REPEAT_MIRRORED([1,0]),
    REPEAT_MIRRORED([0,1])],offset=0.1)`

A useful included module for debugging Bezier curves is `BezierVisualize(p)`.

**Updates:** 

**January 8, 2020:** Remove warning in newer OpenSCAD versions.

**December 12, 2019:** `PathToBezier()` added.

**December 1, 2019:** SMOOTH_ABS() and other functions work together with LINE() on the other side of the node.

title: Playful Faux Fur Wildlife Ears STL File | Elegant Animal Headband for Events & Fun
description:
Transform your look and embrace the charm of the woodland with this exquisitely designed 3D printable realistic deer ears headband. Whether you're preparing for a cosplay event, a themed party, or simply adding a touch of playful elegance to your casual attire, this model offers a unique and captivating accessory.
This meticulously crafted headband features a slim, curved black plastic base, designed to print with a smooth, glossy finish that sits comfortably. Firmly attached to the top are two elegant deer ears, standing approximately 12cm tall, capturing the graceful posture of a real deer. The ears are broad at the base, tapering beautifully to a rounded point, with a subtle, natural cupped shape that enhances their lifelike appearance.
Every detail has been considered to evoke genuine realism. The model is sculpted to simulate the texture of short, soft, realistic brown faux fur on the outside of the ears, contrasting with a delicate, creamy tan velvety lining on the inner ear. These textural cues, though digital, allow for incredible realism when printed and painted, making your finished piece truly stand out. This accessory isn't just a simple print; it's an opportunity to bring a beloved forest creature's charm to life!
Printability & Recommendations:
This model is engineered for an enjoyable and successful 3D printing experience, suitable for various printer types and skill levels.
Printer Type: Compatible with both FDM and Resin (SLA/DLP) 3D printers. Resin printers will excel at capturing the fine textural details and smoother curves, while FDM printers can produce a robust and durable wearable piece.
Material: For FDM, PLA or PETG are excellent choices. PLA offers ease of printing and good detail, while PETG provides extra durability and flexibility, ideal for a wearable item. For resin, standard photopolymer resins will yield superior surface finish and intricate detail.
Layer Height: For FDM, a layer height of 0.15mm to 0.2mm is recommended for a good balance of detail and print time. For resin, utilize your printer's standard high-resolution settings.
Infill: A moderate infill of 15-20% is suggested for the headband and ears to ensure structural integrity and durability, especially for regular wear.
Supports: Supports will likely be required for the underside of the ears where they connect to the headband, and possibly for the inner cupped sections of the ears. Optimize your print orientation to minimize support contact on highly visible surfaces, especially if you plan to paint or flock.
Post-processing: After printing, you can sand the black headband for an even smoother, glossier finish. For the ears, careful painting with various shades of brown and tan, or even applying flocking powder, can dramatically enhance the faux fur effect, bringing the realistic textures to life.
Why This Deer Ears Headband is a Must-Have:
Exceptional Realism: Designed with meticulous attention to detail, from the ear shape to the simulated fur and velvet textures.
Versatile for Any Occasion: Perfect for cosplay, Halloween, themed parties, theatrical productions, photography props, or simply adding a whimsical touch to your everyday outfits.
Print-Friendly Design: Optimized for ease of 3D printing, making it accessible for both beginners and experienced makers.
Unique & Charming: Stand out with a distinctive, nature-inspired accessory that embodies elegance and playfulness.
Unleash your inner forest spirit! Download this high-quality deer ears headband model today and add a unique, charming piece to your collection of 3D printed accessories.
We love seeing your creative prints! Share photos of your finished deer ear headbands with the Cults3D community. If you have any questions or need assistance with printing, please feel free to reach out to us.

title: Flsun QQS Ball Mount Effector
description:
This is my version of the Flsun SR effector and rods for the QQS.  It improves accuracy, reduces noise, and can improve speed.

This design is for the use of 10mm ball stud that are threaded with 4mm threads.  I used 60mm long full thread bolts cut down to approximately 54mm long for the effector, and used 4mm x 12mm bolts for the slide.

The slides are designed for long series LM8LUU linear bearings.  I used these https://www.amazon.ca/gp/product/B083XQTH41/ref=ppx_yo_dt_b_asin_title_o01_s00?ie=UTF8&psc=1 

But this will be up to you. 

I would refrain from using 2 shorts bearing stacked, I tried this and has alignment issues, so a single 45mm long bearing is best.

For the balls, I used https://www.amazon.ca/gp/product/B07HQ72H1R/ref=ppx_yo_dt_b_asin_title_o06_s00?ie=UTF8&psc=1
and work great.

For the Arms,  I used 1/4" aluminum tubes I purchased from a local hobby store.  I cut to a length of 255mm and glued one end on and let cure, I used 2 part 5 minute epoxy.  once cured I used the fixture to set the lengths, do one at a time and the overall length is critical, only use one fixture to make all 6.  this should make 285mm rods.  But measure the best you can for yours and use that for your settings.
author: nkbrisson2
printing_settings:
For the effector, I used PETG-Carbon fiber, as I found this material hold up to the heat, as well is extremely stable dimmensionally.
The rod ends can be made from PETG, Nylon, PLA, printer must be pretty well calibrated as the diameter for the ball cup is tight and may even still require some work to get them a perfect fit.  I used PETG for mine.  And I took a spare ball and used a grinder to cut a slot in it, then mounted in an electric drill to shave the inside of the cup, the fit needs to be perfect, and no resistance to move the ball once installed.
Once you have all printed and installed. Perform calibration and enjoy.

They are made to be printed at 0.2mm layer height, with the three top layers being only the numbers, so you can to a filament swap to a different color.
For the numbers to print, you can't use a nozzle bigger than 0.4mm.
They can attach to the minis with something like sticky tack or a reusable glue like Glue Dots or similar.
My reasoning for this is that they would fit most base sizes in the 25mm range (as they tend not to be 100% consistent).

They are designed in Fusion 360, and I have attached the source files for anyone that wants to make tweaks.

Helmet:

    Head Circumference: Wrap the tape measure around the widest part of the head, just above the eyebrows and ears. Record the measurement as the overall head size.

    Face Width: Measure the distance between the widest points of the face (cheekbone to cheekbone).

title: Skull Jack-O-Lantern Pumpkin Light Up with Bottom Closure
description:
I made this Jack-o-lantern to sit on my mantle for the Halloween season. I designed this to have a bottom closure rather than having a lid with a crack where light can shine through. It has a stem that slides on top, it is a tight fit, so no glue is needed. The bottom has a candle holder plug to hold a battery tea light candle that rotates to secure in place. I used a flickering one to resemble a real candle that is on a timer so I don’t need to manually take out the candle to turn it on.

This is for personal use only. If you would like to sell it commercially, please check out this listing: https://cults3d.com/en/3d-model/home/skull-jack-o-lantern-pumpkin-light-up-with-bottom-closure-commercial-use

These are the candles I used: https://amzn.to/3KBFfI6

Check out my other Jack-O-Lanterns!
https://cults3d.com/en/design-collections/greanbeanz/pumpkins
author: greanbeanz
printing_settings:
I printed the stem with a layer height of .1 to capture as much detail as possible with 3 perimeters and 10% infill. I used tree supports for the stem.
For the pumpkin, I used a layer height of .12, 3 perimeters and 15% infill. If you don’t use enough perimeters and infill, the light will start to shine through the main body of the pumpkin. I painted on build plate only tree supports in specific areas. These are the top of the eyes, the top teeth, the upper corners of the mouth, and then the inside of the flat part of the dome in the ceiling. I imagine it would be a pain to remove supports from all the round parts of the ceiling and mine printed fine without that.
The bottom candle holder piece requires supports under the tabs only.
When you rotate the bottom piece in, don’t force it. You may not have removed all of the supports under the tabs. Make sure you have and then try again. It will be a little snug but you shouldn’t need pliers to untwist it.

title: Macbook Pro Apple Pencil, Post-it and Pen holder
description:
I am Teleworking and have a small desk area to work on.  I had pens shoved here and there under my laptop, keyboard etc..  I wanted to have them accessible and out of the way.
I use a regular keyboard and noticed one day, while looking at my laptop there was plenty of space around the track pad on the macbook with no ports or side speakers.  I thought I could design a simple pen holder to hold my Apple pencil and various pens and pencils.  Even hold my bic white-out roller.

There are five holes for pens or pencils. an area for a standard size post-it pad and two snap ends to snap an Apple pencil onto the end.  The holder slides onto the bottom sides of the laptop.  The holder is designed to slide onto the laptop to the front right side of the track pad.  The holder can also be attached to the other side but the Apple logo cutout will not be shown, which will leave a flat surface for a post-it pad.  This can also be achieved by turning the holder upside down on the right side as well.  The apple pen is attached to the side of the holder by snapping it into the two snap ends on the side ends of the holder. The holder will fit onto a Macbook pro 2018 or any mackbook with a 11mm depth.  I have a Dell Latitude which the holder also fits on snuggly.

There are 4 versions of the holder.  The Ver3 is for non-Apple users who do not want the logo on their laptop real estate.  I have also entered diameters of the holes and pencil holder for those who want to tinker the file to their needs for different pens and stylus's.
author: lemonhead
printing_settings:
Prusa MK3
PLA
.2mm resolution
.6mm nozzle  * Will work fine with .4 nozzle as well.
0% infill, but at least 10% infill with gyroid fill to make it more rigid.  0% infill is no problem but does make the holder easily moveable if the laptop is placed vertically.  Or you can put some pieces of the fuzzy side velcro on one inner side to give it more of a snug fit.
215/70 Extruder/bed
No supports except for those holding the Apple pencil snap ends in place.  These supports are already part of the design, so there is no need to add them in your slicer.  The supports can be easily broken off by hand or nipped off for more aesthetic look.
The diameter of the holes are as follows for anyone who wants to readjust the holes in the stl file.
Bottom 2 holes are 12mm and spaced 88mm from the open end.
Top 5 holes are 11mm and spaced and spaced 89mm from the open end.
The diameter of the snap on Apple Pencil holder is as follows:
Plastic snap is 14mm
Inner void is 8.9mm

Its designed for the Makita DDF482Z, but it will fit on other Makita models as well I think.


It can hold up to 24 bits, but some should be left empty because the bits would get in the way of your hand. So it fits both left and right handed people.





I left 5 empty on the left side (I am lefthanded) and it fits perfectly for me.


I glued some small magnets under it, so the bits dont fall out, because in my case they slide easily in an out.





I added some different version with different sizes of the hexagonal holes (from 6.2mm to 6.9mm). I used the 6.62mm version.

title: Barnum and Bailey no 50 car 1/76 scale
description:
Barnum and Bailey no 50 car 1/76 scale

one of sleeper cars for the European/UK tour 1897 - 1902 .This one had more differences to others and is thought to have been Bailey's private car. 
Based on known measurements and photo of car.

The Barnum and Bailey 'Greatest Show on Earth' toured the UK and mainland Europe , using purpose built wagons and coaches, based o American designs, but reduced in size to fit smaller loading gauge. After the tour finished the stock was used by Buffalo Bill's Wild West Show until 1906, after which the stock was sold off, some to the Alexandra Docks Railway(ANDR), some to a colliery ,but other buyers are not known

Requires chassis, bogies etc.

title: WW2 British 2 Inch HE Mortar Shell
description:
Full size imitation of a British 2-inch high explosive mortar shell used in WW2 + Korea and beyond by Britain and Commonwealth nations  (Australia, New Zealand, Canada etc). It was fired from the Ordnance SBML 2-inch light infantry mortar, which served until the 1980's and also came to be used by quite a few other nations including Jordan, India and South Africa, making this highly relevant to a large number of conflicts.

Has a high amount of detail - fuze with replicated stamping and safety pin hole in case you want to make up the pin + tape for extra authenticity, fuze cap has the 'remove before firing' and arrow indicator instructions modelled on, the fuze cap and tail cap both thread on (I designed extra clearance so anyone can print this successfully), tail has the correct placing and spacing of vent holes + fins with correct profiles.

Prints in 5 major parts with a printable hex rod locking the body and fuze together. Use glue for maximum strength. 3D-printable stencils for markings are included.

Approx. size of complete assy: 240mm (9.5") high and 54mm (2.1") wide at widest point.

Great to use in a display or for British/Commonwealth WW2 re-enactment kit or perhaps one of the other conflicts!

You can find my mortar shells collection  [here on Cults!](https://cults3d.com/en/design-collections/blackswanprints/artillery-shells-and-mortars)
- - -
**UPDATES**
07-Aug-2026 (v2.2 - added 3D-printable stencils for markings)
27-Dec-2024 (v2.1 - adjusted clearances for better fit)
- - -
(Note: This is a cosmetic imitation only, it cannot function or be made to function as a real device. I am not responsible for any mis-use of the printed items. The renders showing paint colours and markings are for
illustration purposes only - I don't provide stencils or paint guides.)
author: blackswanprints
printing_settings:
Printer with minimum 145mm Z-axis (height) print space required!
Consumes ~135g of filament when using recommended settings.
0.20 layers with 5% infill recommended for most parts, print the fuze + tail caps with 0.12mm layers to ensure threads print correctly.
Parts pre-oriented in best printing position. The fuze cap will require supports underneath. If you don't want the cast instructions on the top of the fuze cap, I provided a 'clean' STL that does not have them, which allows it to be printed upside down without supports.

title: TMNT 1989 带石版的街机柜
description:
This piece is representative of the original TMNT 1989 Arcade Cabinet.

Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles, released in Japan as TMNT: Super Kame Ninja and in Europe as Teenage Mutant Hero Turtles, is a 1989 beat 'em up arcade game released by Konami. 
It is based on the Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles franchise, including the first animated series that began airing two years earlier. 
In the game, up to four players control the titular Ninja Turtles, fighting through various levels to defeat the turtles' enemies, including the Shredder, Krang and the Foot Clan. 



This is a 2 piece set, composed of the arcade cabinet itself and it's base. I've shown an example in the pictures how we can light up this piece, but take into consideration that we can use the light according to your own creativity (different colors, intensity, position, etc.).

Behind the piece you will find a small hole just in case you want to use a light source with a cord (e.g. LED strip).

Construcción en PLA estándar:
Gracias a su diseño optimizado, el dron ofrece una excelente resistencia estructural incluso cuando se imprime en PLA común. Esto permite que su frame soporte caídas y choques habituales sin comprometer su integridad. Aunque no es indestructible, su robustez lo hace ideal para uso frecuente.
Para una mejor durabilidad recomendamos imprimir en ASA a 145 grados y una cama a minimo 60  , su resistencia aumenta un 200x100
Vuelo versátil: suave en interiores y potente en exteriores
Este dron ha sido cuidadosamente ajustado para ofrecer dos modos de vuelo diferenciados. En interiores, brinda una experiencia de vuelo suave y controlada, ideal para espacios reducidos. En exteriores, se transforma en una máquina ágil y potente gracias a una configuración de PIDs, tasas y rates específicamente calibrada para ofrecer un rendimiento más agresivo. Cambiar entre ambos perfiles permite adaptarse fácilmente a distintos entornos y estilos de vuelo.
Compatibilidad total con Betaflight
El dron es 100% compatible con Betaflight, lo que permite una personalización completa de todos los parámetros de vuelo. Desde PIDs y rates hasta filtros y modos de vuelo, todo puede ser ajustado a gusto del piloto. Esta compatibilidad ofrece una plataforma ideal tanto para quienes buscan afinar al máximo el comportamiento del dron como para los que están aprendiendo y quieren experimentar con diferentes configuraciones.
Montaje económico: solo 39 €
Una de las grandes ventajas de este dron es su bajo coste. El montaje completo tiene un precio total de apenas 39 euros, lo que lo convierte en una opción ideal para quienes buscan iniciarse en el hobby sin invertir demasiado, o para pilotos experimentados que quieren un dron funcional, económico y fácil de mantener. A pesar de su bajo coste, ofrece un rendimiento sorprendente gracias a su diseño optimizado y componentes bien seleccionados.
Lo mejor de todo: este precio no impide que mire de frente —y en más de una ocasión le moje la oreja— a algunos productos comerciales bastante más caros.
Modos de vuelo para todos los niveles
Este dron es capaz de volar en los tres modos clásicos de Betaflight: Acro, Horizon y Angle, lo que lo hace ideal tanto para principiantes como para pilotos avanzados. This also allows you to use this base model with the add-ons without needing to reprint parts you have already made! printing_settings:
Assembly Note
Some parts of this bundle are recommended to use glue – the year and doorknob specifically.  The rest of the pieces will stay with gravity.
If you have issues with fit, please feel free to reach out to me and I will be happy to assist you. If your machine does not have very precise or accurate tolerances, you may want to scale the models up or adjust your precision settings.
Scaling down model will not work as the tolerances will likely be too small for the pieces to fit.
For most accessories for this gnome, you will be required to remove a hand or hands to place the accessory in the gnome’s hands.  Glue is not needed for most of the parts of these models.  We do recommend it when you want permanent adhesion of for certain small parts.
Print tolerances vary by printer. The settings used in this print were in Bambu Studio, and printed on a Bambu X1C using a 0.4 nozzle printed at 0.20mm layer height Standard print quality settings. Filament used was PLA and PLA+. Plate used was Bambu Textured PEI Plate.
Adding variable height, ironing or smaller layer heights will decrease the visibility of any lines even more than what is shown in the photos.

title: Advanced Skimmer System for your 30mm Sand Filter System or Intex Pool Pump
description:
This project is regularly updated.





Newest Version September 01, 2024





Two 3D printable skimmer systems for your 30mm sand filter system or pool pump and three different jets.





"Why buy an expensive skimmer system when you can build a better one yourself for €11 in materials costs?" was my thought.





Newest version is all together in one piece and even fits a regular filter cartridge from intex or else!





Older version with perfectly floating surface dirt collector and floor dirt collector.





For the older version you need a DN40 HT pipe of the appropriate length, sawn to length if necessary, and a step drill to attach and glue the "pool outlet" into the pipe. You also have to glue the "PoolRohr" pieces together.


You should use a hand saw to cut at least 8 10mm deep slots into the HT pipe, which should then be around 1mm wide. You can deburr the slots with a lighter.





Glue everything with a petg capable glue.


Ive used 2K resin glue and superglue with activator.


Roughly sand the areas to be glued before sanding.





Before drilling and assembling, measure the exact height of your water outlet in the pool. and the height of your surface so you can make sure the surface collector will always rest in the lowest position in calm water.


Make sure the floor nozzle will hover at least 2cm above the floor.





Have fun swimming and happy printing.

title: Model Railway Portable Wheelchair Ramps
description:
This is a design that I had been thinking of doing for a while but never sure how best to design it so it was fairly easy to print. After a request from a customer and the improvement in resin printers I decided to give them a go.

After a bit of research I decided I needed to do three version. 

1: In the unfolded position. 
2: In the folded postion for carrying. 
3: In the wall locked away position.  

The ramps are approximately 24mm long, 5mm wide in folded position and 10mm wide in the open position.

This item has been designed at OO gauge, 1/76 scale.
for HO gauge print at 87%, 1/87 scale,
for O gauge UK print at 175%, 1/43.5 scale,
for O gauge American print at 158%, 1/48 scale,
for N Gauge UK print at 51.5%, 1/148 Scale, (Caution: I have not test printed this in N gauge scale).

The example in the pictures was printed on an AnyCubic Mono 4 Ultra 3D resin printer.
I recommend printing these on a 3D resin printer to get the best print definition.
As per normal with my designs, there is a balance between accuracy and printability, hopefully not affecting the look of the model too much.

I use AnyCubic Water Washable Resin for most of my items, but use AnyCubic ABS Like Resin for anything that needs to be stronger and tougher.

This is the resin I recommend. ANYCUBIC Water Washable Resin 2.0 https://amzn.to/48TL8vs (Affiliate Link)

_**Additional Info**_

Please check my Website, **https://sites.google.com/view/pete3dprintinghelp/home**

My website has lots of useful info.

If you like my content and would like to buy me a coffee to say Thank You, then please click this link https://ko-fi.com/petes3ddesigns

The top (25% infill) and Handle (100%) and straps (100%) will use about another 1.5kg.

Disable supports and change "Build plate adhesion" to none

author: abbymath
printing_settings:
Stand bases are approximately 113x 53 x 245 mm (Trapezoidal) and 104 x 40 x 25 mm (Rectangular). The short inserts are 91.4 x 82 x 4.4 mm and the tall inserts are 91.4 x 112 x 4.4 mm. (Blank ones are 3.4 mm thick.) The text is 1 mm thick, so color swaps work well at 3.4 mm height.
I printed the bases with 0.25 mm layer height, 3 perimeters, 3 top and bottom solid layers, and 10% infill. The inserts were printed with 0.25 mm layer height, 2 perimeters, 3 top and bottom solid layers, and 15% infill.
For the texture on the inserts, I modified the top layer of the plate to print with 80% or 65% honeycomb infill and no top layers. I also modified the top layers of text to print with 1 perimeter so there is more room for external infill. For the "14" I used an additional modification to create the outline by printing the very top layer with 2 perimeters, 0 top layers, and 0% infill. This insert was done with two filament swaps on a single-color machine.
No supports. No raft.
Reminder: If you add your own text or logos to the blank plates, don't put it too low and obstruct insertion into the base.
Not for commercial use. No derivatives. See © link.

title: tpu battery holder
description:
Too many loose batteries?  Print a couple of these to organize them and hold them together.  This was designed to be printed in TPU, it probably won't work right for non-stretchy material. 

This will probably work for any cylindrical battery, but I've only tested with sizes AA and AAA.

You can also choose hexagonal or square (not pictured) packing.  You can make a set of rings for almost any number of batteries.  I've included a variety of shapes and sizes, or you can change the numbers to make the size you want.  Note that the hexagonal arrangement has one extra battery in every other row, so a 3x3 hexagonal grid holds 10 batteries.

This currently only supports a rectangular grid arrangement, but I may add circular and triangular arrangements if someone says they want them.  (Or other arrangements if suggested.)

I printed this with Sainsmart TPU (shore hardness 95A) which make the overall part surprisingly strong and rigid while individual rings are still stretchy and flexible.

title: Fully Articulated Mechanized Colossus
description:
Bring the legend to life with the Fully Articulated Mechanized Colossus — a towering dieselpunk war machine of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, now engineered with full articulation for dynamic posing, display, and customization. This is not just a model — it’s a functional, poseable figure, blending ornate historical aesthetics with brutal battlefield engineering.

Standing over 125mm tall with its iconic spire helm, this mechanical giant is clad in riveted armor adorned with Polish-Lithuanian heraldry. Every joint is fully articulated — from its rotating turret head to its massive arms and stride-ready legs — allowing you to recreate heroic stances, mid-battle swings, or commanding poses.

Armed with a colossal flanged mace capable of leveling fortifications, the Colossus can switch between head options:

Ornate Spire Helm — evoking the grandeur of a war-chapel on legs.

Winged Hussar Helmet — giving the machine a knightly, aggressive silhouette.

Both options retain full articulation, letting you create the perfect battlefield presence for your collection, wargaming army, or display shelf.

Whether for tabletop dioramas, dynamic display, or stop-motion projects, the Fully Articulated Mechanized Colossus delivers unmatched versatility and presence.

Included in this set:

Fully Articulated Mechanized Colossus STL (125mm tall with spire helm / 110mm with Winged Hussar helm)

Fully poseable joints for arms, legs, torso, and head

Swappable head system (spire helm and Winged Hussar helm)

Ornate armor with Polish-Lithuanian heraldry

Towering flanged mace weapon

66 separate parts for assembly and articulation

Important:

title: Angela Merkel – Caganer Style Figure | 3D Printable Figurine

This 3D printable figure presents Angela Merkel interpreted in the traditional Caganer style, a well-known European folk art form characterized by humorous and satirical figurines. The model features a crouching pose, simplified proportions, and a recognizable formal outfit, blending political iconography with playful artistic expression.

The design focuses on clean geometry and print reliability. Facial features, clothing folds, and body proportions are intentionally simplified to ensure smooth FDM printing while preserving the character’s likeness and iconic presence. This model is ideal for collectors, novelty displays, and cultural figurine collections.

⚠️ Important Notes Before Printing:

The model is provided at a generic default scale. Please adjust the scale before printing depending on whether it will be used as a small figurine or a display piece.

The base is solid and integrated, providing stability during printing and display.

No fragile elements are present, making the model suitable for single-piece printing.

title: Decorative Butterfly Illustration - Wall Art Multicolor
description:
# Decorative Butterfly Illustration - Wall Art Multicolor

**Thank you for checking out my design.**  
If it helps you, please **Follow** and **Like** so you don’t miss future uploads.  
Free models and contact: https://makerworld.com/en/@BrunoBarros

---

## What’s included
- **Multicolor wall art**: two STLs (black + white).
- **One-color wall art**: one combined STL (relief).

---

## Multicolor printing
- Import **both** STLs into your slicer as parts of the **same object** (center them together).
- Assign different colors/filaments to each STL.
- To remove details, **split into parts** in your slicer and delete what you don’t need.
- Want a simple silhouette? **Import the black STL alone** and print single color.
- If the white layer has small floating bits you don’t want, **split the white STL into parts** and delete the loose ones, then print what remains (you can also recolor remaining parts to black if desired).

---

## One-color printing
- Use the **combined STL** for a single-color relief look.
- To get two-tone without AMS, add a **pause at layer height** at the color change and swap filament manually.

---

## Tips
- Scale freely; models are vector-derived and print well at multiple sizes.
- Typical FDM settings work: 0.2 mm layer height, 2–4 walls, 10–20% infill.  
  Adjust to taste for speed vs. detail.

---

## Support & questions
Questions or requests? Message me on MakerWorld: https://makerworld.com/en/@BrunoBarros  
You can also reach out here on Cults3D.

title: Logitech G27 Load Cell Mod Mount & Adapter
description:
Created this in 2017 but have forgotten to share it here. Try my best to describe below. 

Please print at min 50% infill or best yet 100% infill because I don't how much of force you gonna excert at those. So far mine didn't brake yet

Some of the articles you can find about making the circuitry that reads the load cell signal for your G27 as below. If i rmbr well each of this circuit has its own hiccup such as spike(at least for me, but maybe not you), in the end i got a friend to custom the board for me with very similar components but much smoother signal and adjustment.
- https://chippedwood.wordpress.com/2015/07/07/46/
- http://cbtechnical.blogspot.com/2011/04/amplifier-circuit.html

- https://www.racedepartment.com/threads/diy-project-wip.98008/

The load cell i used is a generic 20kg one that you can get anywhere. Length of 130mm x 30mm. Has mounting holes of 15mm apart horizontally. I would recommend to get at least 30kg. There load cell in the market that has different hole configuration, mine is the one in the rendered pic, or such as below that matches the dimension,
20kg - https://www.ebay.com/itm/Parallel-Beam-Load-Cell-Sensor-20kg-45lb-Weight-Sensor-with-Shielding-Cable-CE/181118193076?hash=item2a2b7c4db4:g:SX0AAOSwmtJXXVIo:rk:18:pf:0

title: Samsung Galaxy A01 a015 case
description:
Originally published [here on Thingiverse](https://www.thingiverse.com/thing:6036636).

Thanks to [Victor Bernal](https://cults3d.com/en/users/mattrumble) who helped me testing this case. Some of the models are designed for rigid materials and others for flexible ones. **The models materials are not interchangeable**, so pay attention to the file names. If you have any request on the design just ask me.

For other phone cases check [this](https://cults3d.com/en/design-collections/tato_713/phone-and-akin-cases-73dd).

Here is the explanation of the files names:

- **Flex:** made for elastic filaments like TPU. Not tested.
- **Rigid:** made for rigid (non-elastic) filaments like PLA, ABS, HIPS, etc. The entire model is a little bigger and the holes for the buttons are opened on the front side. Tested only on PLA.
- **Banded:** It has regular horizontal grooves in the bed surface, to make the finished texture more regular, avoiding irregularities on that part, and bringing it a better grip.

References
-------

- [GSMArena](https://www.gsmarena.com/),

title: MATCHSTICK LIGHTER
description:
https://youtu.be/33qXOuM4LJs

I was playing with a modern gas lighter some month ago Suddenly I thought of something
Before this madden gas lighter was invented, the matchbox was the first thing
Then I thought that the fuel of the first lighter must have been a match
I immediately searched the internet for the first developed lighter
But I was shocked that the lighter was invented before the matchbox
Yes A chemist named Johann Wolfgang Döbereiner invented the first lighter in 1816
Then in 1827 John Walker invented the matchbox in England
Well I searched the internet again after 1827 to see if anyone had made a lighter using a match as fuel and nope. 

Then I had a playful idea that if I had been born in 1827 I would have done this
Immediately I decided to make it now I decided that it should be as it would have been if it had been developed in the 19th century
I decided it should be in a historical design 
For this I used my spare time for three months After several hundred prints it has become perfectly formed
Now the world's first match stick lighter has been developed I was very happy 

 You can make it in PLA and PETG filament If you want to work for a long time then choose PETG
There are 19 stl giles in total, also opj If you want separate files please download separately
Or as a whole but also as a whole You can download as per your choice

 I have also attached a video on youtube showing how to assemble it accurately If you see it, anyone can assemble it very easily, so I have made a video to make it easy to understand
Give it a try, you'll love it, thanks

1 dragon body

5 right horn

6 matchstick holder

11 clip [print it two pieces ]

12 small screw [print it two pieces ]

rom the 1st stl to the 8th stl you should use 20% infill density or or more of your choice,From the 9 to the 19 file you must use 100% infill density

Design Concept
The Chibi Mermaid Statue features a cute and whimsical design, embodying the playful essence of chibi art style. Its friendly appearance is crafted to captivate and bring joy to enthusiasts of mythical creatures.

Purpose
Designed primarily for decoration, this model is ideal for placement in creative spaces or as part of a themed collection. It can also serve as a charming gift for lovers of fantasy elements and small statutes.

Printing Recommendations
For best results, print using a resin printer to capture fine details such as the mermaid’s scales and facial expressions. A fine layer height of around 0.05mm is suggested to maintain the intricacies of the model. Supports are necessary to ensure the stability of the fins and hair during printing.

Depending on the size of the print bed, the statue might need to be printed in parts and later assembled with an adhesive. Dry-fit before finalizing to ensure seamless attachment.

title: Amarox Wireless BBQ Meat Thermometer Battery Cover
description:
One of the ears on the battery cover of my Amarox Wireless BBQ Meat Thermometer broke off, so I whipped up a model in FreeCAD and voila. This is an older model than what is currently available on Amazon, but someone out there might have this same model. 

Print Advice:
I suggest printing this in the orientation presented. Yes, it will require extensive supports, but it is necessary for strength so that the tabs don't break when flexed. Also, due to the small footprint in this orientation, I recommend a brim of 7mm. I printed it in PLA, but due to the fact that it will be near a barbecue grill, you might want to opt for ABS, PETG or even PLA+ might work better.

title: Royal Pod Stand
description:
Royal Pod Stand is a premium interior plant pot featuring a refined vertical texture and a raised structure. The stand with legs adds visual lightness and turns the plant into a focal point of the interior.

Balanced proportions and a versatile design make it ideal for modern, Scandinavian, and minimalist interiors. It works equally well with decorative greenery, flowering plants, and cut flowers.

The model consists of separate elements:

the vase (main pot),

the stand,

four legs.

The legs attach to the stand, forming a stable and reliable structure. All parts are printed separately, making the 3D printing and assembly process easy and convenient.

The package includes two file versions:

a version with drainage holes — suitable for soil and live plants;

a version without holes — suitable for holding water and using as a flower vase.
